in rats with bile obstruction, a decrease in glucose level is associated with an increase in fructose-2,6-P2 and hexose monophosphate levels, indicating that the block at the level glucose production is responsible for the decrease in plasma glucose level and for the activation of fructose 6- phosphate-fructose 1,6- bisphosphate futile cycle.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impairment of hepatic gluconeogenesis in the starved state may be the main reason for the hyperinsulinemia in the rats with bile duct obstruction, which is a model of human cholestasis.
the impairment of hepatic glucose output is the primary event in bile duct ligated rats, and the impairment of gluconeogenesis and the activation of the futile cycle are secondary events.

the block of glucose production by the impaired gluconeogenesis and the activation of the glycolysis by the increase of fructose-1,6-biphosphate and fructose 2.6-bisphosphatase activities may contribute to the development of hypoglycemia in rats with bile obstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

bile duct ligation is an excellent model to study the regulation of hepatic carbohydrate metabolism, and it is a useful tool for the investigation of the mechanisms underlying the regulation of hepatoportal glucose metabolism.
bile duct ligation causes an impairment of hepatic carbohydrate metabolism, especially in a starved condition.
